meta_title: For parents — The Lord of the Rings 2026
description: What the event is, from what age children can take part, safety, documents and equipment. A practical guide for parents of children and younger participants.
title: For parents
subtitle: When your child is heading to Middle-earth.
ch_signup: How to sign up the child
intro_p1_pre: If your child has convinced you they want to come to
intro_p1_strong: The Lord of the Rings — Battle for Middle-earth
intro_p1_post: , you’re in the right place. Here you’ll find an overview of what the event is, from what age children can take part, how we handle safety, what documents we need and what the child should bring.
intro_p2_pre: The Lord of the Rings is a big weekend
intro_p2_strong: LARP inspired by J. R. R. Tolkien’s world
intro_p2_post: . Participants pick a side and an army, prepare a costume, weapon and character, and live a story together in the world of Middle-earth. They get camp life, programme, roleplay, costumes, community and above all the Saturday battle.
intro_p3_post: and run by people with long experience of similar events.
h_larp: What LARP is and what combat looks like
larp_p1: LARP is a game played live. Participants aren’t just spectators — they enter the story themselves. They put on a costume, play a character and engage with what’s happening according to the rules.
larp_p2_pre: Combat is part of The Lord of the Rings. We don’t fight with real weapons. We use
larp_p2_post: , typically swords, axes, spears, shields or bows, which must pass an organiser check. The weapons are not metal and they are designed to be as safe as possible for play.
larp_p3_pre: Even so, it’s good to expect
larp_p3_strong: an active outdoor activity in the terrain
larp_p3_post: . People run, fight, play outside and in the forest. A scrape, bruise, fall or sprained ankle can happen. Serious injuries at events like this aren’t common, but they can’t be entirely ruled out — same as with sports, summer camps or other outdoor activities.
medic_pre: A medic is present in camp throughout the event. Details:

vek_p3: People under 15 may take part only accompanied by a person over 18 who is responsible for them during the event. It can be a parent, legal guardian or another adult with whom participation is clearly arranged in advance.
vek_p4_pre: If the child isn’t coming directly with a parent, we need it in writing
vek_p4_strong: who is responsible for them at the event
vek_kids_p1_pre: For younger children we are preparing a separate
vek_kids_p2_pre: It is mainly for children roughly aged
vek_kids_p2_post: . Younger children, roughly aged 3 to 5, can only join with a parent or another responsible adult.
vek_kids_p3: The children’s game is not a substitute for looking after very small children. It’s a programme for young adventurers — safer, more playful and adapted to their age.
h_alone: When the child travels without parents
alone_p1: If you’re sending an older child to the event without you, please check the following:
alone_l1: the child has a valid registration,
alone_l3: they have a printed and signed application / legal guardian’s consent,
alone_l4: they have a health insurance card,
alone_l5: they have an ID or other identity document if they already have one,
alone_l6: they know who their adult escort or supervisor is,
alone_l7: they have any necessary medication and know when to take it,
alone_l8: any health information is reported to the medic at registration,
alone_l9: they have suitable equipment for the camp, the forest and the weather,
alone_l10: they understand they must respect the organisers’ instructions.
alone_p2: It’s important for children and younger participants to know that a simple rule applies at the event:
alone_p3: It isn’t that we want to ruin the adventure. It’s so that the game stays safe, fair and manageable for everyone.
h_with: When you travel with the child
with_p1_pre: You can come with the child as a
with_p1_post: . You can be in camp, watch from a safe distance, help the child with equipment, rest or orientation on site.
with_p2: You can also take part more actively. You can register as a playing participant, choose a side and an army, prepare a costume and live the weekend fully alongside everyone else.
with_p3: If you come only as an escort, we still ask you to respect the atmosphere. Ideally, wear simple, non-distracting clothing in natural colours, perhaps with a cloak, tunic or another basic costume element. You’ll help maintain the impression of Middle-earth and won’t look like a 21st-century guest in the camp.
take_l1: a costume in which the child can move safely,
take_l2: a safe foam-padded weapon that passes the safety check,
take_l3: gloves (don’t underestimate them — your unbruised fingers will thank you),
take_l4: a helmet or suitable head protection for younger / smaller participants,
take_l5: sturdy, non-distracting footwear suitable for the forest,
take_l7: their own water bottle or canteen,
take_l8: a sleeping bag, sleeping pad and other camping gear,
take_l9: a snack and something quick for an energy boost,
take_l11: a signed application / parental consent if the participant is under 18,

kids_p1: The children’s game is a programme for younger children who can’t yet join the main battle, or for families who want to enjoy the event together.
kids_p2: We are preparing activities adapted to children roughly aged 5 to 10. It can include team games, small tasks, crafts, movement activities, simple riddles, forest stations, archery, drawing, a path of courage or small story scenes.
kids_l1_post: a team game on the meadow for children who arrive earlier,
kids_l2_post: games, crafts, forest activities, archery, obstacles and workshops,
kids_l3_post: a short path of courage ending with a scene,
kids_l4_post: the main children’s game across stations,
kids_l5_post: further more relaxed activities depending on the situation and the children’s energy.
kids_note: The exact programme may still change based on weather, number of children and organisational possibilities.
kids_box_p: Sign up the child or read the programme details.
h_battle: Can I go to the main battle and leave the child at the children’s game?
battle_p1: Yes, for children of an appropriate age we plan for this. If the child can manage the programme on their own, they can take part in the children’s game while the parent goes to the main game or battle.
battle_p2: For younger children, however, we need the parent or an arranged adult escort to be nearby and step in as needed. For children roughly aged 3 to 5, parental escort during the children’s game is required.
battle_p3: We will be very glad if parents also help directly with the children’s game. Small things help: assisting at a station, escorting a small group, handing out water, calming a young adventurer or supporting the atmosphere of the game. Every bit of help counts.
h_signup: How to sign your child up for the children’s game
signup_p1: The child needs to be signed up via the registration system.
signup_p2_pre: If the whole family is coming, register at least one parent and add the children as associated persons via the registration system. Then sign them up to the section / side
signup_p3: If you’re not sure, write to us. Better to sort it out in advance than to have confusion at arrival.
signup_box_p: Registration form for the whole family.
family_fee_p1_pre: We don’t want family participation to be unnecessarily off-putting. That’s why we have set a
family_fee_p1_strong: maximum cap on the registration fee for a family
family_fee_p2: If several members of one family are coming, please check the current conditions during registration or write to us. We’ll help you choose the right approach so that registration meets the rules and makes sense for family participation.
h_zazemi: What will be available on site
zazemi_l6: an arranged inn / on-site catering, depending on current information,
zazemi_p2: On the other hand, don’t expect normal modern comforts. Electricity, showers, good mobile signal and convenient charging may not be available.
zazemi_note: It’s a weekend in Middle-earth — beautiful, adventurous, but still outdoor and camp-style.
park_p1: If you arrive by car, please follow the organisers’ instructions. Parking will be marked and you must respect where you can and cannot drive.
park_p2: If a parking card is required, print it, fill it in and place it behind the windscreen.
park_p3: The roads to the venue may be forest tracks, dusty or harder to drive on. Drive slowly and considerately — both for the people and nature, and for your own suspension.
faq_a1: We do our best to make it safe. We check weapons, work with combat rules, and have a medic and organisers in the field. At the same time, this is an active outdoor event where a minor injury can happen.
faq_q2: Can the child come on their own?
faq_a2: Players from age 12 may take part in the main game. Up to age 18 we need a signed legal guardian’s consent. People under 15 must be accompanied by someone over 18 who is responsible for them.
faq_q3: Does the child need a costume?
faq_a3: Yes. The costume is part of the game and the atmosphere. It doesn’t have to be perfect, but it should match the chosen army, be safe and usable in the terrain.
faq_q4: Does the child need their own weapon?
faq_a4: If they want to take part in combat, yes. The weapon must be padded and pass the check. We recommend having a backup option in case a weapon doesn’t pass approval.
faq_a5: Yes. You can come as non-playing escort, as a playing participant, as a helper, or you can help us with the children’s game.
need_p1: The most important thing is that the child doesn’t arrive “just like that”.
need_l6: an arranged supervisor if the child isn’t coming directly with you,
need_l7: a basic understanding of the rules and safety.
need_p3: If you’re not sure, write to us in advance instead. We’re a band of adventurers, but in these matters we like things clear.

end_p1: The Lord of the Rings is a weekend full of stories, costumes, battles, friendship and camp atmosphere. For children and younger participants it can be a strong experience — an adventure that stays in memory for a long time.
end_p2: Please help us by preparing the child well, equipping them properly and explaining the basic rules. We’ll make sure they don’t get any more lost in Middle-earth than is healthy for a good story.
cta_p: Middle-earth is a big world — and all the better explored together. If you’re not sure, write to us.
take_l14: a good mood and a willingness to play fair.
